title: Inside cover and first page: entries 554, 642, 647 of 1837

entries.abstract: Left side: blank inside cover with pencilled shelf numbers.

Károly Werfer, bookseller of Kassa (Košice), is printing a Hungarian edition of a French work, "A friendly examination of the English Church and of the Reformation in general". The bishop urges the clergy to subscribe and wants at least one copy bought for each district. Names of subscribers are due by the start of August. Countersigned as revised by the vice-archdeacon.
Arising from the conversion of Carolus Vajna, a Unitarian from the Transylvanian diocese: because the form of Unitarian baptism is in doubt, such converts are to be baptised conditionally.
Passes on a Lieutenancy Council notice of 11 July (no. 21502) about the Institute for the Blind in Pest and its endowment, with an appeal for gifts. Continues on the next page.

transcriptions.label: Entry 554, opening lines
transcriptions.original: Dilecti in Christo Filii! Carolus Verfer Bibliopola Cassoviensis opus sub titulo: Barátságos Visgálat az Angol Egyházról, és általyában a Reformatioról praelo subjicere intendit. In optima spe, quod opus istud Scientiarum Amatoribus, et Ecclesiae Catholicae Cultoribus plene satisfacturum sit [...] Datum Szathmarini die 22a Junii 1837. Joannes mp. Episcopus Szathmariensis. Revisum per V.A.D.D.
transcriptions.english: Beloved sons in Christ! Károly Werfer, bookseller of Kassa, intends to send to press a work titled "A friendly examination of the English Church and of the Reformation in general". In the best hope that this work will fully satisfy lovers of learning and those devoted to the Catholic Church [...] Given at Szatmár, 22 June 1837. Joannes, Bishop of Szatmár, in his own hand. Revised by the vice-archdeacon of the district.

title: Entry 909 of 1837, theses for 1838, entry 115 of 1838 (fee tariff)

entries.abstract: Administrative circular about a named individual and a legal claim. Subject not securely read.

Questions every priest must answer in writing during 1838, in dogmatic, moral and pastoral theology and canon law, followed by the topics for oral examination at the spring, summer and autumn district meetings (among them the divinity of Christ, public instruction, natural, divine and human law, and the authority of councils).

Uniform tariff of stole fees for the whole diocese, issued because the faithful kept complaining about what they were charged. Items listed: churching after childbirth, each reading of banns, weddings (priced by the couple's social standing), baptismal, banns and marriage certificates, burials (priced by standing), funeral sermon. Individual amounts in kreuzer are legible only in part.

title: Entries 280, 333, 519 of 1838 and a local gift note

entries.abstract: Dating clause of the fee tariff.
Rules for district libraries, with the Ungvár district library as the case in point: where it is kept, who acts as librarian, a catalogue, loans of four weeks, and a yearly account.
List of works bought to enlarge the Ungvár district library, mostly Hungarian-language sermons and devotional theology.

Death notice for the grand provost and canon of the cathedral chapter, Joannes Nepomucenus (surname not read), who died on the 9th. Career as told: seven years a military chaplain, including the Belgrade campaign under Laudon; then parish work; canon from the founding of the chapter in 1804. Masses requested.

The noble Miss Theresia Kulin gave a red silk veil worked with flowers, "to the praise and glory of the name of Jesus". Entered in the book so the gift is remembered. Her place name, written "de K. Sz...", may be Kis-Szeretva (Stretavka), a village near Senné.

title: Entry 626 with the Eger missing-husband notice; entry 715 begins

entries.abstract: At the request of Carolus Rajner, vicar of Eger, the clergy are to search for Ludovicus Szathmáry and report the result. The Eger letter is copied below it.

A young Jewish man, son of Abraham Levi and Eva, born in Szatmár county, moved to a village in Heves county, was baptised there on 15 June 1823 as Ludovicus Szathmáry and married Catharina Tóth on 10 July of the same year. After six years and four children he left home at the start of July 1829 and never returned or wrote. His wife believes he tired of home life, went back to his former religion and returned to where he came from. Description: short, lean, long pale face, black hair, a weak left eye; speaks Hungarian, Slavic and Romanian besides his mother tongue.
Long pastoral instruction on mixed marriages between Catholics and Protestants: the dangers the bishop sees, and how priests are to counsel couples. Continues over the next two pages.

transcriptions.label: Copy of the Eger notice, 11 July 1839
transcriptions.original: Illme &c. Juvenis quidam hebraeus Parentibus Abrahamo Levi, et Eva cujus cognomen ignoratur in Possessione [Cottus?] Szathmár Bi[...] natus. Inde ad Possessionem [Cottus?] Heves [...] delapsus, ibi anno 1823 15a Junii baptisatus, die vero 10a Julii anno eodem cum puella [...] Catharina Tóth nuptias celebravit. Exactis in Matrimonio annis 6 generatisque prolibus 4, vir hic sub initium Julii 1829 [...] domo discessit et hoc tempore nunquam remeavit, nec de ubicatione sua uxori suae ullum nuncium misit. Afflictae conditionis uxor [opinatur?] virum curarum domesticarum pertaesum ad nativam Religionem delapsum esse; locumque Originis [...] Szathmár, aut vicinos Comitatus in quibus cognatos fors habet, repetiisse [...] mentionatum virum, a tempore suscepti baptismi nomine Ludovici Szathmáry vocitatum [...] Est vir hic staturae parvae, macilentus, oblongae pallidae faciei, nigricomus, ad sinistrum oculum lippus, loquiturque praeter nativam, linguas hungaricam, slavicam ac valachicam. Agriae 11a Julii 1839. Carolus Rajner mp.
transcriptions.english: Most Illustrious Sir, etc. A certain young Hebrew, born to Abraham Levi and Eva (her surname is not known) in a village of Szatmár [county]. Having drifted from there to a village in Heves [county], he was baptised there on 15 June 1823, and on 10 July of the same year he married a girl [...], Catharina Tóth. After six years of marriage and four children, this man left home at the beginning of July 1829 and has never since returned, nor sent his wife any word of where he is. The wife, in her distress, [believes?] that her husband, weary of household cares, has lapsed to his native religion and gone back to his place of origin in Szatmár, or to the neighbouring counties where he may have relatives [...] the said man, called Ludovicus Szathmáry since his baptism [...] He is a man of short stature, lean, with a long pale face, black-haired, bleary in the left eye, and he speaks, besides his native tongue, Hungarian, Slavic and Wallachian. Eger, 11 July 1839. Carolus Rajner, in his own hand.

entries.from: Compiled family-tree chart (derivative source, author unknown)
entries.abstract: A printed family-tree chart, in colour, titled 'Rodostrom rodiny Javorovej' (family tree of the Javor family), with the word 'náhľad' (preview) stamped across it several times. About 250 name boxes in eight or nine generations, a coat of arms, eleven photographs and two churches. At this size only the lowest three generations and the photograph captions can be read at all. No Duska is legible anywhere on it. One ancestor is legible in part: Mary D[an]ko or D[em]ko, born 1906, died 199[?], whose box appears to give a birthplace in the U.S.A. and a line naming Vysoká nad Uhom. Her parents' boxes read Andrej D[..]ko and Mária M[...]ová, both with Vysoká nad Uhom. The younger generations are living people and are not abstracted here.

transcriptions.label: The one photograph caption that bears on either line, as far as it can be read. Square brackets mark doubtful letters.
transcriptions.original: Mary D[an]ko [or D[em]ko] 1906 - 199[?]
transcriptions.english: Mary Danko or Demko, 1906 to 199[?]. The Demko agent reads a 1991 on the chart as the death year of her son, and the last figure of hers as unclear. The surname has five letters, begins with D and ends in -ko; the two in the middle cannot be told apart at this size. The image is not published because the chart shows living people with their dates of birth. Its file name and SHA-256 are given so that the copy can be checked.

entries.abstract: Child: Mihály, born 3 July 1903, baptised the 4th, legitimate. Father: András Duska 'the younger' (if.), Roman Catholic, cottar, of Szenna. Mother: Anna Nyemecz, Roman Catholic, of Szenna. Residence: Szenna, house 79. Godparents: János Hreha, Greek Catholic, cottar; Anna Laskodi, Roman Catholic, both of Szenna. Officiant: Gyula Buzinkay, parish priest. The remarks column is empty: no death is noted, where this book notes the deaths of four of his brothers and sisters. House 79 is the house of the mother's parents in 1866 to 1872. A candidate for Michal Duska, Ahn 8 (H-046).

entries.abstract: 'Worth remembering. The series of parish priests of the church of Szenna, as far as it could be dug out of old documents, the registers especially, after the church was recovered from the Calvinists in 1718.' Twenty-six priests follow, from Adamus Petrik to Georgius Balás (1850 to 1886), among them Stephanus Rácz, 1831 to 1841. Under Balás: windows repaired, a new organ bought; on 28 October 1865 at eleven at night something was destroyed by fire 'through a malicious man'; a bell was blessed on 20 July 1871 by Bishop László Bíró in honour of St Ladislaus, with a bell for Solymos dedicated to St Christopher. Then, in later hands: Julius Buzinkay made interim administrator; Stephanus Rusznák named administrator on 4 October 1886, invested 1887, died 3 May 1892; Buzinkay took the place on 24 July 1892 and was invested on 7 November 1894. The image carries a microfilm target reading 'Whole Volume'. Much of the lower half is at the limit of legibility and is given only in outline.

transcriptions.original: Memoria digna. Series Parochorum Ecclesiae Szennensis in quantum erui poterat ex antiquis documentis signanter Matriculis post recuperatam a Calvinis 1718. Ecclesiam haec erat: Adamus Petrik. Paulus Zaleganus. Georgius Frater a 22. Octobr. 1720 – 18. Septm. 1729. Georgius Kiresi a 1729 – 1730. 22. Mai. P. Joan. Joseph. Benedicti a 1730 – 1731. 7. Jun. P. Joann. Joseph. Zaffian a 1731 – 1735. 23. Jan. P. Georgius Kohut a 1735 – 1736. 18. April. Nicolaus Bacsik a 1736 – 1740. quo Szennae mortuus. Emericus Kolocsanyi a 1741 – 1742. 28. Octobris. Joannes Jasztrabszki a 1742 – 1743. 6. Julii. P. Joannes Ulrich a 1743 – 1748. 9. Octobr. Paulus Habinák a 1748 – 1753. P. Paulus Fries a 1753 – 1756. 15. Augus. Georgius Konjan a 1756 – 1759. 11. Jul. Joannes Moroli a 1759 – 1762. 14. April. Adamus Bribóczy [?] a 1762 – 1778. Martinus Leporisz a 1778. Joannes Zsigmondovics minorita 1779. P. Clemens Kripsik minorita 1779. usque 10. Octob. Stephanus Kellercsik a 1779 – 17[82] 6. Junii. Martinus Majercsik a 1782 – 18[25] 4. Maji quo Szennae mortuus. Martinus Behák a 1825 – 1828. Josephus Seigel a 1828 – 1831 quo discessit ad Jenke ubi mortuus 1854. Stephanus Rácz a 1831 – 1841 [...]. Josephus Harkel a 1841 – 1850 [...]. Georgius Balás a 1850 – 1886. Sub quo reparatae fenestrae, novum [...] erectum, procuratum novum Organum, [...] 1865. 28. Octobris hora 11. nocturna [...] per malignum hominem igne absumptis [...] Campanae [...] 1871. die 20. Julii benedicta per Illmum Eppum Ladislaum Biró in honorem S. Ladislai, una cum Campana Solymosiensi dedicata honoribus S. Christophori [...]. Julius Buzinkay cooperator Szennensis constitutus est pro Interim[ali] Administratore. Stephanus Rusznák [...] 4. Oct. 1886 [...] nominatus est pro administratore Szennensi. Investituram obtinuit [...] 1887. [...] mortuus die 3. Maji 1892 [...] Julius Buzinkay [...] Accepit locum die 24. Julii 1892. Investituram obtinuit die 7. Novembris 1894 [...]

entries.from: Parish burial register, page image (original record), low resolution
entries.abstract: A two-page spread of a handwritten burial register with Hungarian headings: date of death and of burial, name, age in years, months and days, illness, and manner of burial. The surnames on it (Kenderes, Kudrócs, Knyezso, Dzvonyik, Kolyibás) are those of the Reformed baptisms of Solymos in folder F-007, so this is taken to be the Reformed burial book of the same place; the image carries no title. Two entries name the family. Under 1833, no. 3: György Dusko, buried 27 February, aged 29. Under 1838, no. 2: Pál Duska, buried in May, aged 68; the illness reads as dropsy (vízibetegség) and he was buried 'with a sermon' (tanítással). The image is small and the writing is at the limit of what it will bear: names and ages are read, days and causes are doubtful. Pál Duska, born about 1770, is the oldest person of the surname in the archive.

entries.from: Newspaper report (derivative source, printed far from the event), as a print from a newspaper archive
entries.abstract: A one-page print of a clipping from an Ohio newspaper, the Telegraph-Forum of Bucyrus, 17 January 1911, page 4, read in full at B-026. A report from Niobrara, Nebraska, dated 16 January: the gas lighting plant of the Hubbard hotel exploded and killed M. W. Kimball, Annie Duska, Kenneth Kindall and R. F. Crosby; four women were rescued from the fire, which burned the hotel. Nothing in it says where she came from, how old she was or whose kin she was. A Nebraska paper of the same week names the hotel's owner as Michael Kendall and lists among the dead 'Ann Duseka, a cook' (lead L-021), so the Ohio wire copy garbled at least one name and her surname is spelled two ways. The file is held because its footer carries the owner's account name on the newspaper site; the report itself is transcribed here whole.

W. Kimball, Annie Duska, Kenneth Kindall and R. F. Crosby. Four women were rescued from the flames that followed the explosion and burned the hotel.

entries.abstract: The second page of the table for Solymos, a village of the first class, where a full holding is 20 holds of arable and 10 mowers of meadow. It carries the running total forward, then lists serfs 27 to 29, housed cottars 1 to 9 and sub-cottars 1 to 8, all of the first landlord. The owner's file name says an 'Andref Duska' is here. The only András on the page is sub-cottar no. 8, and his surname is read here as [B]utka, not Duska: the first letter is not the D the same clerk writes in 'Duska Mihály' on the next page, and there is a t where the s should be. Housed cottar no. 9, György, has the same surname, and he cannot be the György Duska who is housed cottar no. 10 on the next page. The image is small and the reading is low, so this is a hypothesis (H-058), not a finding. The printed columns are: name; size of the holding as a fraction of a full one; house plot in Pozsony measures; arable in holds; meadow in mowers; days of labour a year with draught animals, or instead days by hand; the ninth; then yearly dues: rent in florins, firewood in cords, spinning in pounds, clarified butter in icce, capons, chickens, eggs.

entries.abstract: A printout in French from a cemetery's records system, made on 2 January 2022. Deceased: Duska, given name written Mikalis. Date of birth 28 November 1890. Spouse: Anna Hancosek. entries.abstract: A printed colour map of Ung county, drawn by Pál Gönczy, at 1:380,000, with relief, rivers, marsh, roads, the railway and the four districts outlined in red. It gives the county's area as 3,052.84 square kilometres and its population as 135,247, which dates it to the 1890s. For this archive it shows three things. Solymos and Szenna are neighbours, about 4 km apart by the map's scale, with marsh between them. The red district line runs between them: Solymos, Jesztreb, Rebrin and Gézsény lie in the Szobránc district, and Szenna, Pályin, Viszoka and Csicser in the Kapos district. And Lasztomér, the home of the carpenter János Demko's wife, lies just over the county line in Zemplén. Any record kept by district, a census among them, will have the two villages in different bundles.

entries.abstract: A black-and-white school map of Ung county issued for the minister of religion and education, dated 1915 in the corner, with the population of 1910 (162,089) and six districts. Someone has since added a small coloured square on every village: red across the south around Nagykapos and Csap, green across the west around Szobránc, purple through the mountains and the east, a few striped or dotted. The image has no key to the colours; by where they fall they look like the main language of each village (Hungarian, Slovak, Ruthenian), and that is this agent's inference, not something the map says. Solymos, Ungszenna, Rebrény, Gézsény and Magasrév are green; Csicser is red. Two names matter here. Szenna is 'Ungszenna', the form the Senné register takes up between 1903 and 1906. And where the older map has Viszoka, this one has Magasrév: the birthplace written on the Demko agent's 1906 record is Viszoka under its new name.

entries.abstract: A typed and signed Québec government form, the declaration of a civil marriage. On 11 October 1984, at the Palais de Justice in Montréal, Kevin Duska, single, born in Montréal in 1962, married Lyne Lefebvre, single, born in Montréal on 4 July 1964, French-speaking. The groom's father is entered as Steve Duska, born in Czechoslovakia, and Steve J. Duska signs as a witness. This is the first document in the archive for the link between Kevin's father and his grandfather Štefan. The bride was Kevin's mother; he states that she has died, so her name and the marriage are shown (S-000-10). Still withheld, and blacked out on the published copy: the groom's day and month of birth, the couple's address and the groom's signature, because Kevin does not know whether his father is living; the bride's parents and the groom's mother, who belong to lines outside this experiment and whose status is not known; the second witness; and the official.

entries.abstract: A printed court form, typed in. The district court at Michalovce, acting as guardianship office, file Nsl 446/37, consents on 7 October 1937 that the minor Štefan Duško, born 23 October 1929 at Senné, may emigrate in the company of his mother, Mária Dušková née Demková of Iňačovce, to Canada, to his father Michal Duško. The mother may sign the transport contract in the guardian's place. The reasons: the father asked for it, the boy will be fully provided for with him, and the escort is over 24 years old, wholly reliable, and has bound herself in writing to take him all the way. The surname is typed Duško throughout. The boy's birthday is given as 23 October; the parish certificate of 1947 has 21 October. Nothing is said of the father's age or of where in Canada he was.

entries.abstract: A household sheet of the Czechoslovak census of 1930, printed in Slovak and Hungarian and filled in in Hungarian: Beša, district of Veľké Kapušany, house 1[0]4, owner Ignác Schwarcz, for the night of 1 to 2 December 1930. Seven people, three generations. Ignác Schwarcz, house owner, born 2 March 1865, married, a merchant on his own account, in the village since January 1870. Fanny, his wife, born 8 August 1868, married in September 1886, mother of eight children of whom two are entered beside it. Lipót, their son, born 1 January 1888, married, a merchant. Hermin, their daughter-in-law, born 21 September 1894, married on 6 January 1920 and in the village from that day. The grandchildren Vilmos (8 March 1921), Edit (6 December 192[3]) and Tibor (6 October 1926). All are Czechoslovak citizens with their home commune at Beša; nationality is entered as Jewish and religion as Israelite; the adults read and write. There is no Duska and no Demko on the sheet. The owner's file is numbered 1 and his folder is called 'whole', so this is all he kept from Beša. The only Schwarz in this archive is Erzsébet Schwarz of Alsó-Ribnicze, the Catholic wife of György Duska the younger of Senné; nothing on this sheet connects the two.

entries.from: Census household sheet (original record, screen capture)
entries.abstract: House 145, owner Andrej Duška, on the night of 1 to 2 December 1930. Andrej Duška, head, born 24 November 1868 at Senné, married, a farm day-labourer who can neither read nor write. Anna, his wife, born 24 August 1872 at Senné, married on 18 January 1892, mother of twelve children of whom nine are living; she can read. Juraj, their son, born 2 March 1910, single, a day-labourer. Maria Dušková, 'daughter-in-law of the head', born 15 August 1907 at Iňačovce, Greek Catholic, married on 30 January 1927 and living in Senné since that day. Štefan Duška, 'grandson', born 23 October 1929 at Senné, Roman Catholic. Maria's husband is not in the house. This is the record that names Michal Duska's parents. Štefan, born 23 October 1929, son of a Greek Catholic Maria from Iňačovce, is the Štefan of the 1937 passport and court consent, whose father was Michal. He is entered as the grandson, and his mother as the daughter-in-law, of Andrej and Anna, married 18 January 1892: the András Duska and Anna Nyemcsik of the marriage entry D-006-03, whose son Mihály was baptised on 3 July 1903 (D-009-79). Maria's date of birth here, 15 August 1907, differs from her passport's 22 August 1906; her father-in-law, who could not read, was probably the informant.

transcriptions.english: House 73. Jozef Duška, farmer on his own land, born 29 May 1885 at Senné: the József baptised that day, son of György Duska the younger (FG-48). His wife Anna, born 5 May 1890, Greek Catholic, married 22 January 1910, mother of five; children Anna (1921), Ján (1923), Maria (1925); and her mother, the widow Anna Chalahánová, also called Pošíková, born 9 December 1858. House 73 is the house András Duska lived in from 1893 to 1907; by 1930 it is his kinsman Jozef's.

title: Passenger list: Mikulas Duska, 39, and Michal Duska, 26, of Senné, arriving in Canada, [1929 or 1930]
span: [between Nov 1929 and Jul 1930, from the ages]

provenance.archive: unknown; a Canadian passenger list by its form and its naturalisation notes
provenance.book: Passenger list, ship and date not shown
provenance.obtained: From the owner's folder 'AAAA Unclassified', through the Sorter's pile 'to-duska' in the private repository at commit 73cf83d (Sorter batch S-B-017). An enlarged crop; how the owner obtained it is not recorded.

entries.abstract: An enlarged crop of a typed passenger list of men arriving in Canada, with later notes by the immigration office. Three men in a row are from Senné, Czechoslovakia, Slovak: Andrey Dzvonik, 24; Mikulas Duska, 39; and Michal Duska, 26. The ship, the port and the date are not in the crop. Against Michal an office hand has written 'Copy on O.F. 633695' and 'Nat. 22/4/40': a copy of the entry went to file 633695, and he was naturalised on 22 April 1940. That file number is the one on the Immigration Branch letter of 1937 to Mike Duska of Montréal (D-006-11, read there as 6336[93]), so this Michal is Štefan's father. Against Mikulas: 'Nat: 21/1/46'. Between the two lines a hand has written what looks like '+ Brother'; the typed relationship column has only ditto marks under 'none'. The ages date the voyage: a man born on 3 July 1903 was 26 until July 1930, and one born on 28 November 1890 was 39 from November 1929, so they sailed between late November 1929 and early July 1930, within months of Štefan's birth. entries.from: Newspaper death notice (derivative, supplied by the family; print from a newspaper archive)
entries.abstract: A death notice from The Montreal Star of Saturday 2 February 1974, page 10. Mike Duska, Sr., died at the Montreal General Hospital on 31 January 1974, aged 71. He was the husband of the late Mary Demko, the father of Steve and Mike, and the grandfather of Kevin. The funeral was on Monday 4 February from the Slovak church of St. Cyril and Method, with burial in Côte-des-Neiges cemetery, where his wife's stone stands. This is Michal Duska, Ahn 8. A man born on 3 July 1903 was 70, not 71, on that day; a family's count a year out is ordinary. The notice shows a second son, Mike, not met in any earlier record; he was not on his mother's passport in 1937, so he was born in Canada after that. The 'Sr.' is for him. The image is held; the notice is given here in full.

entries.from: Parish extract of a baptism entry (derivative, sealed)
entries.abstract: A second extract of the same register entry as the certificate of 1947 (D-X01-01): Senné Roman Catholic baptisms, volume IV, page 110, entry 43 of 1929. Štefan, born 21 October 1929, baptised 26 October, legitimate son of Michal Duška, cottar, Roman Catholic, of Senné, and Mária Demko, Greek Catholic, of Iňačovce; parents' home Senné 160; godparents Jozef Macko-Kocák, student, Greek Catholic, of Michalovce, and Zuzanna Bandura née Hankoščák, Roman Catholic, of Senné; baptised by Ján Barna, parish priest. Issued at Senné on 1 October 1955, eight weeks before Štefan's wedding in Montréal. Two things it settles: the church's date is 21 October, written by two priests eight years apart, against the 23rd of the civil papers; and the godmother is clearly Zuzanna, born Hankoščák, the family of Mikuláš Duška's wife.
